But here’s the thing: it’s not affecting the things I enjoy right now, is it? You might argue, “Well, it might in the future.” And while that is a possibility, we shouldn’t jump to the conclusion that it inevitably will.

Let’s take a look at the example someone mentioned about 4kids altering and censoring anime. Yes, they altered and censored some shows, but not every anime was subjected to censorship. If we fast forward to today, we can see that anime isn’t experiencing widespread censorship anymore, right? (Unless we count “people complaining on Twitter” as censorship). So if our fear of sweeping censorship didn’t come true back then, why do we assume it will undoubtedly happen now? Moreover, I want you to know that censorship has happened to things I liked, and I wasn’t thrilled about it either. You know what I did? I simply stopped supporting those things and moved on to other things I liked. Yes, I was annoyed that they censored aspects I enjoyed, but it wasn’t the end of the world.

Now, you might argue, “But these changes are pointless/stupid.” I totally agree with you on that. It’s frustrating and maybe even infuriating. But here’s the thing: even though I agree, it’s not enough for me to worry incessantly about potential censorship. We’ve witnessed far worse censorship in the past, and chances are we’ll see more in the future. Usually, it’s much more obvious and overbearing. So, in this case, it’s simply a matter of not liking certain changes, and that’s perfectly okay.

Lastly, you may ask, “When will the censorship stop, then?” It's quite difficult to tell with certainty, but rest assured, it always stops somewhere. Remember that the slippery slope argument, although it may seem convincing, is still a fallacy.

Rewrite and format the following commentary (on “create” of Genesis 1:1) keeping as many of the same words as possible:

The Hebrew word for “create” (bara’) is used in the OT to refer to divine activity only—YHWH alone serves as its grammatical subject—in doing, or calling into existence, something new or marvellous: cf. Exodus 34:10; Isaiah 40:26. In the present section it occurs again in connexion with (1) the creation of living organisms (Genesis 1:21); (2) the creation of man (Genesis 1:27); (3) the creation of the whole universe (Genesis 2:3-4). It is used in Psalm 148:5 where the reference is to this section. A different word, “made” (‘asah), is used in connexion with the “vaulted dome” (Genesis 1:7), the heavenly bodies (Genesis 1:16), the terrestrial animals (Genesis 1:25). It is, however, a mistake to suppose that the word bara’ necessarily means “to create out of nothing”; it often stresses forming anew, reforming, renewing (see Ps 51:10; Isa 43:15; 65:17).

What rhetorical strategies are being used here: A quarter of a million people, human beings who generally had spent their lives treated as something less, stood shoulder to shoulder across that vast lawn, their hearts beating as one.
Hope on the line. When hope was an increasingly scarce resource.
There is no dearth of prose describing the mass of humanity that made its way to the feet of the Great Emancipator 2 that day; no metaphor that has slipped through the cracks waiting to be discovered, dusted off, and injected into the discourse a half century on. The March on Washington has been compared to a tsunami, a shockwave, a wall, a living monument, a human mosaic, an outright miracle.
It was all of those things, and if you saw it with your own eyes, it wasn't hard to write about.
With that many people in one place crying out for something so elemental, you don't have to be Robert Frost to offer some profound eloquence
Still. I can say to those who know the event only as a steely black-and-white television image, it's a shame that the colors of that day-the blue sky, the vibrant green life, the golden sun everywhere -are not part of our national memory. There is something heart-wrenching about the widely shown images and film clips of the event that belies the joy of the day. But it could be worse. We could have been marching in an era before cameras and recording devices, then the specifics of the event would eventually fade out of living memory and the world would be left only with the mythology and the text. Text without context, in this case especially, would be quite a loss. One might imagine standing before an audience and reading Reverend Martin Luther King, Jr's "| Have a Dream" speech verbatim, but it is a stretch to believe that any such performance would sow the seeds of change with, as Dr. King put it that day in Washington, the
"fierce urgency of now." The vast crowd, the great speaker, the words that shook the world-it all comes as a package deal. We are truly fortunate to have a record. Yet what the television cameras and radio microphones captured that August day is but a sliver of the vibrancy of the event. When a film adaptation of a beloved novel premieres, the people who say "Oh, but you've got to read the book" are inevitably right. The density of the written word makes the flat motion picture a pale artifact in comparison. In a similar fashion, although watching the black-and-white news footage of Dr. King's historic call to action is stirring to almost everyone who sees it, learning about the work that went into The March and the speech-the discussions and debates behind closed doors -offers a unique context that magnifies the resonance of hearing those famous words " have a dream" in that phenomenal, inimitable cadence.
If taken together, the images and recordings of Martin make up that "movie" of the 1963 March on Washington in our collective consciousness, and if it's true, as people often say, that "If you loved the movie, you've got to read the book," Behind the Dream is that book. It is a story not known to the general public or disclosed to participants in The March -or, in fact, to many of its organizers. I acquired private truths and quiet insights during the months leading up to this historic event. For the most part, I've kept them to myself. But as this book is published, I will be entering my eighth decade on this Earth, and as I move closer to the final horizon, I realize the time has come to share what I know. The experiences cannot die with me; the full truth is simply too important to history.

However, ticks have developed excellent cold hardiness ability to overcome the negative effect of cold stress (Yu et al., 2014). Previous studies suggested a series of biochemical changes including water, glycerol, fat, and protein content were observed during cold hardiness in ticks (Yu et al., 2014; Wang et al., 2017). A recent study showed the involvement of diverse genes including the aquaporin, ferritin, superoxide dismutase, heat shock protein (HSP), and cold shock domain protein (CSDP) families during the cold response of ticks (Yu et al., 2022; Rosendale et al., 2022). Additionally, it was suggested that epigenetic regulation of DNA methylation plays an important role in the cold hardiness of ticks (Agwunobi et al., 2021; Nwanade et al., 2022).

from openpyxl import Workbook
from openpyxl.styles import Alignment


def fill_sheet(sheet, sites):
    """
    Fill the excel sheet with missed cells.

    Args:
        sheet: openpyxl sheet object
        sites: list
    """
    if len(sites) == 0:
        return
    columns = [
        'Region',
        'ENM',
        'ERBS_Name',
        'ID',
        'eNBId',
        'Vlan',
        'VlanRef',
        'ExtEnodeB VlanRef',
        'EranLink',
        'PTP Time Sync',
        'Elastic Ran LKF',
        'Elastic Ran Feature',
        'BBU',
        'Port Bitrate',
        '10G LKF',
        '10G Feature',
        'EUtranCells',
        'Eran EUtranCells',
    ]

    row = 1
    for col in columns:
        cell = sheet.cell(row=row, column=columns.index(col) + 1)
        cell.value = col


    row = 2
    for site in sites:
        for col, cell_val in site.items():
            col_index = columns.index(col) +1
            cell = sheet.cell(row=row, column=col_index)
            cell.value = str(cell_val)
        row += 1


def fill_excel(sites, path):
    """
    Fill excel file with missed in atoll cells, each technology to separate sheet.

    Args:
        selected_data: dict
        path: string
    """
    work_book = Workbook()

    work_sheet = work_book.create_sheet('ElasticRan')
    fill_sheet(work_sheet, sites)

    del work_book['Sheet']
    work_book.save(path)

Вместо этого каждый участник находит свое место в качестве временного лидера на определенном этапе проекта, соответствуя своим лучшим компетенциям и способностям. После завершения этапа, лидер сменится на следующего подходящего участника. Это позволяет равномерно распределить ответственность и обязательства, и обеспечить наилучшее использование возможностей каждого участника проекта. Однако, для успешной реализации такой концепции, все участники группы должны быть на одном уровне интеллектуального, культурного, социального развития, уметь эффективно общаться и владеть навыками лидерства и эффективной работы в команде.
Принцип распределенного лидерства, основанный на делегировании управленческих функций при решении общих задач, позволяет достижение более высоких показателей эффективности, по сравнению с традиционным монолидерством. Он осуществляется путем того, что каждый участник команды имеет возможность использовать свои лидерские качества и компетенции в зависимости от конкретного этапа проекта. Такой подход не только позволяет эффективно использовать ресурсы команды, но и повышает мотивацию ее участников, благодаря ощущению своей значимости и принадлежности к проекту.

The term "postmodernism" refers to a number of artistic and literary movements that emerged in the 1970s in opposition to or rejection of the dogma principles or practices of established modernism. History of Postmodernism
The term was initially used in a number of contexts in the 1870s. As an example, John Watkins Chapman promised "a Postmodern style of painting" to go beyond French Impressionism. Then, J. M. Postmodern Art and Literature
Often described as a style or movement that originated in the decades after World War II, postmodernism in literature is typified by its significant emphasis on methods like fragmentation, contradiction, and problematic narrators. Postmodern literature is often seen as a backlash against Enlightenment ideals and Modernist techniques.

Sir Isaac Newton (1642-1727) was an English scientist
who made great contributions to physics, optics, maths
and astronomy. He is known for his Three Laws of Motion
and the Universal Law of Gravitation.
When Sir Isaac Newton was a boy, he was more
interested in making mechanical devices than in studying.
He made a windmill which could grind wheat and corn,
and he made a water clock and a sundial. His teachers
thought he was not a very intelligent student because he didn’t do very well.
He wanted to go to college, but he didn’t have the money to go, so at university,
he had to serve the other students by doing chores for them. He even ate the
leftovers of their meals, but he would do anything to get an opportunity to learn.
Even when he was in college, he was not outstanding and received no awards.
When the university shut down because of the plague, an illness where people
caught diseases and died suddenly, he went home and continued to study on
his own.
He had a notebook with blank pages and he began to fill them with notes as he
read and experimented about different things around him.
One day, when he was drinking tea in the garden, he saw an apple fall to the
ground. He started thinking about why it fell. Why did the apple fall out of the
tree? Does everything fall? What makes things fall? Can anything stop things
from falling? Are the sun, moon and stars falling? Why don’t they ever fall to the
ground? He finally decided that a force called gravity, which cased the apple to
fall also kept the moon in the sky around the Earth. This same force called
gravity, also kept the planets in the sky around the sun.
The apple incident led to his three basic laws of motion:
 A moving object keeps moving unless an outside force stops it.
 An object moves in a straight line unless some force makes it change
direction
 For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.
Isaac Newton is well known as one of the greatest scientists who ever lived.

翻译：A trivial approach for the selection mechanism consists of
checking for the inclusion of selection points coordinates in
each objects’ area. Even with a linear complexity, processing
2,500,682 objects involve a large number of computations. A
pixel is selected by pointing to it with the mouse on the
screen. To determine the object(s) to select, a projection of
the coordinates of the selected pixel must be performed in the
OpenGL 3D space [4] (Fig. 4). This operation produces in a
straight line along the Z axis. Once the projection line is
known, it is possible to compute the intersection between this
line and the objects present in the OpenGL scene. If an
intersection is detected, it means that the object involved is
pointed to and should therefore be selected. To accelerate this
step, some objects could be indexed by the areas they cover.
In that case, the selection is faster, but memory consumption
increases with the index size.

Céline Dion's sister shares update on singer's health amid battle with stiff-person syndrome
Emlyn Travis
Fri, August 4, 2023 at 11:34 a.m. GMT-4·2 min read

Céline Dion's sister shares update on singer's health amid battle with stiff-person syndrome
Céline Dion's sister Claudette is giving an update on the singer's health amid her battle with stiff-person syndrome.

The 55-year-old Canadian pop star announced last December that she would be cancelling her 2023 Courage World Tour dates after being diagnosed with the rare neurological disorder, which causes intense muscle stiffness and body spasms. Now, her sister is sharing how dedicated the "My Heart Will Go On" singer is to her recovery.

"When I call and Céline is busy, I talk to my sister Linda, who lives with her, and who tells me she's working hard," Claudette said in a statement to Le Journal de Montréal translated from French. "She listens as much as possible to the great researchers of this rare disease."

Valentino : Front Row - Paris Fashion Week - Haute Couture Fall/Winter 2019/2020
Valentino : Front Row - Paris Fashion Week - Haute Couture Fall/Winter 2019/2020
Pascal Le Segretain/Getty Celine Dion

Still, Claudette explained that she thinks her sister needs "rest most of all," adding, "She always goes above everything. She always tries to be the biggest, the strongest. At some point, your little heart and your little body speak to you. It is important."

Thankfully, her family is there to support Dion on her journey. "We trust her," Claudette said. "It's in her. She's disciplined in everything she does in her life."

In May, Dion announced that she was officially canceling her 2024 Courage World Tour dates due to her continued health concerns. "I'm so sorry to disappoint all of you once again. I'm working really hard to build back my strength, but touring can be very difficult even when you're 100 percent," she said in a statement. "It's not fair to you to keep postponing the shows, and even though it breaks my heart, it's best that we cancel everything now until I'm really ready to be back on stage again."

Dion added, "I want you all to know I'm not giving up, and I can't wait to see you again!"

The singer previously postponed her 2022 Courage concert dates due to "persistent" medical issues. The move came one year after she postponed her return to her Las Vegas residency, citing medical issues.

The family unit’s essentail role is a recurring theme on the silver screen. For example, director Wes Anderson is a master of portraying the unbreakable family bonds that persist through all manner of hilarious friction and dysfunction. In the outlandish characters of “The Royal Tenenbaums” and “The Life Aquatic with Steve Zissou,” we recognize aspects of our own family’s idiosyncrasies. Stories of orphans, such as “Annie” and “Les Miserables,” have also deeply affected generations of viewers. For both filmmakers and moviegoers, the importance of family is firmly rooted in the psyche.

Across the ocean, Asian family values are famous for a strong sense of belonging and duty. Ang Lee explores these themes in “Eat Drink Man Woman,” in which a father and his three daughters go through individual struggles as fast-paced modernity encroaches on traditional life. A decade and a half later, Stephen Chow directed “CJ7”, a comedy about a poor single father and son who mutually teach each other big life lessons.

No matter which side of the globe, the family nest of love and support is a prevalent basic need.

Family ties may be universally significant, yet there are both subtle and overt differences between cultural expressions of kinship. The film “My Big Fat Greek Wedding” poked fun at cultural clashes between Mediterranean and American family values, yet comparing East to West is an even bigger can of worms.

Western ideals are sometimes synonymous with “liberal”, owing to a cultural heritage of individaulistic philosophy rooted in Ancient Greece. Western education and parenting tend to emphasize independent thinking, encouraging kids to question and form their own opinions. Teenagers are likely to have part-time jobs, postpone college, travel abroad and move out of their parents’ homes by their early twenties.

Emphasis on respecting tradition and ancestors has resulted in quite a different set of cultural norms in Asia. Intensive memorization defines education, and “helicopter parents” feel  entirely responsible for their children’s lives well into their offspring’s adulthood.

In fact, regardless of geography, the more traditional the family , the more pressure is put on the younger generation to follow a prescribed life path, including choice of education, career and spouse. Yet modern transformations of the family unit are on the rise, including interracial and same-sex partnerships. Although the definition of “family” is ever-expanding, affection and mutual support remain the cornerstones. Could friends one day enjoy legal family status? Only time will tell.

(As I walked to the clubroom, I couldn’t believe what happened yesterday. MC, my childhood friend, had died. The news hit me like a ton of bricks. And as I entered the clubroom, I could see Monika and Himari discussing something. Kotonhoa was also there, and was moving a strange pool - it was round and pink. Yuri was there, too - she was filling the pool with warm water. I was confused as to what they were doing, but was even more confused as to where Natsuki was.)

Yuri: “And…that should be everything!”

Monika: “Great job, Yuri. I’ll set up the decorations now.”

Himari: “I’m so excited for this pool party! It’s going to be so much fun!”

Kotonoha: “I hope everyone likes my special punch!”

(I cleared my throat to let them know I was there.)

Sayori: (trying to keep my voice steady) “Hey guys.”

(They all turned to look at me with sad expressions.)

Monika: “Sayori, how are you holding up?”

Sayori: “I’m…not doing well. MC’s death is still a really hard pill to swallow.”

Yuri: “We understand, Sayori. We’re all grieving. But we thought it might be good to distract ourselves with a pool party.”

Himari: “Yeah! We’ll have food, drinks, music, and swimming! It’ll be a blast!”

Kotonoha: “And don’t forget my special punch! It’s delicious!”

Sayori: (forcing a smile) “That sounds like a lot of fun. But…I’m not sure I’m in the mood to party.”

Monika: “We understand, Sayori. But please, try to have some fun. It’s what MC would have wanted.”

Sayori: (nodding slowly) “Yeah…you’re right. MC was always the life of the party. He wouldn’t want us moping around.”

Himari: “That’s the spirit! Now, let’s get this party started!”

Yuri: “Hold on. Does anybody else notice a lack of somebody?”

Kotonoha: “You’re right, Yuri. Where’s Natsuki?”

Monika: “I haven’t seen her all day. Has anyone tried contacting her?”

Sayori: “I texted her earlier, but she hasn’t replied.”

Himari: “I hope she’s okay.”

(Just then, Natsuki burst into the room - and immediately got into the pool, putting a hand on her massive belly. I was thoroughly confused as to why.)

Natsuki: (panting) “Sorry guys, I’m late. I just had to take care of something important.”

Monika: “Natsuki, are you okay? You look exhausted.”

Natsuki: “I’m fine. Just a little tired.”

Yuri: “And why are you in the pool already?”

Natsuki: (looking down at her belly) “Oh this? I just wanted to cool off. It’s been really hot today.”

Kotonoha: “Natsuki, are you sure you’re okay? You seem a bit…different.”

Natsuki: (smiling) “I’m fine, Kotonoha. Just a little pregnant, that’s all.”

Himari: (gasping) “Pregnant? Natsuki, that’s amazing!”

Sayori: “Congratulations, Natsuki! That’s wonderful news!”

Monika: “We’re so happy for you!”

Yuri: “Yes, congratulations.”

Kotonoha: “I can’t wait to make some special punch for the baby shower!”

Natsuki: (in severe pain) “F-F-Forget throwing a baby shower! I think I might be having cramps!”

(Everyone was immediately concerned and rushed to help Natsuki out of the pool. Yuri quickly grabbed a towel and wrapped it around her.)

Monika: “Are you okay, Natsuki? Do you need to go to the hospital?”

Natsuki: (gritting her teeth) “I-I don’t know! I’ve never had cramps before!”

Himari: “Here, lean on me. We’ll get you some help.”

Kotonoha: “I’ll call an ambulance-”

Natsuki: "I'm just joking, guys. I was acting out the birth scene from the manga I'm working on."
